chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said:

Durays was married to the daughter of Ḥumrān, and he stipulated for her that he would not marry another wife over her, nor take a concubine over her, ever during her life nor after her death, on the condition that she stipulated that she would not marry after him. They placed upon themselves obligations of hajj, sacrificial offerings, vows, all the wealth they owned for the poor, and every slave they had to be free, if either of them did not fulfill for the other what had been agreed.

Then he came to Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned that to him. So he said: “Indeed, the daughter of Ḥumrān has a right, but that will not cause us to refrain from speaking the truth. Go, then marry and take a concubine, for that is nothing.”
After that, he came and took a concubine, and afterward children were born to him.

key_terms.ابْنَةُ حُمْرَانَ: the daughter of Ḥumrān, Durays's wife mentioned in the case
key_terms.النُّذُورِ: vows pledged as penalties if the agreement was broken
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: hajj obligations invoked as part of their conditional pledge
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth; here, the Imam's declaration of the correct ruling
key_terms.الْمَسَاكِينِ: the poor, designated as recipients of their wealth
key_terms.ضُرَيْسًا: Durays, the man at the center of the report
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجَ: to marry; here, to take another wife

ai.seo_question: Are conditions in marriage that forbid a husband from ever marrying again or taking a concubine legally binding in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a marital agreement in which each spouse bound themselves to conditions regarding remarriage, together with severe financial and devotional penalties for non-fulfillment. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that although the wife has rights, such a stipulation is not binding in a way that makes the lawful unlawful, and he instructs Durays to marry and take a concubine if he wishes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4484 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurara, who said:

Durais had married the daughter of Humran, and he made a condition for her that he would neither marry another wife nor take a concubine over her, neither during her lifetime nor after her death. In return, she made a condition that she would not marry anyone after him.
They also pledged that if either of them failed to fulfill their commitment, all their wealth, possessions, and slaves would be given as charity to the poor, and their slaves would be set free.

Then, Durais went to Abu Abdillah (as) and mentioned this matter to him.
Imam (as) said: "The daughter of Humran has her rights, but that will not prevent us from speaking the truth. Go and marry and take concubines, for this agreement has no binding effect."
After that, Durais married and took a concubine, and children were born to him afterward.
